references.text: The institution of the Passover celebration in Egypt, where the Lord commands Israel to keep the Passover in the month of Aviv, which is the background for the commandment in Deuteronomy.
Moses reminds the people that they left Egypt in the month of Aviv, confirming the timing of the Exodus from Egypt.
The commandment to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Aviv, when Israel left Egypt.
Reiteration of the commandment regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Aviv, as a memorial of the Exodus from Egypt.
Detailed instructions concerning the Passover celebration and the Feast of Unleavened Bread as part of the Lord's appointed feasts.
The commandment to keep the Passover at the set time, in the first month.
Regulations regarding the Passover celebration in the first month, on the fourteenth day.
Israel celebrates the Passover after entering the Promised Land, fulfilling the commandment.
King Hezekiah restores the Passover celebration in Israel.
The returnees from exile celebrate the Passover following the rebuilding of the temple.
Jesus celebrates the Passover with his disciples, as a fulfillment of the Old Testament feast.
Paul refers to Christ as our Passover lamb who has been sacrificed and urges believers to keep the feast with unleavened bread.
